approach: The block is in equilibrium with only two forces on it, so the incline's total push (normal plus friction combined) must be equal and opposite to gravity.

steps.text: The block is at rest, so only two forces act on it: gravity mg straight down, and everything the incline exerts on it — its normal push and its friction — combined into one net contact force.
Since these are the only two forces and the block is in equilibrium, the incline's net force must be equal and opposite to gravity.
This holds for any θ and μ as long as the block truly stays at rest; the normal and friction parts individually depend on θ and μ, but their combined vector always equals mg.

common_mistakes.text: Reporting only the along-incline friction component, mg sinθ, as the total force from the incline, forgetting to combine it with the perpendicular normal component.
